title: Stock Market Today, S&P 500 Futures Rise 1.27% in Rebound
summary: S&P 500 futures rose 1.27% and Nasdaq 100 futures 1.8% ahead of Friday's short session, as Treasury futures slipped and copper firmed.
body_markdown:
Wall Street snapshot (sources: Investing.com, Saxo) Index Wednesday close (Nov 25) Futures by 21:18 ET Thursday


S&P 500 -0.25% +1.27% to 7,287.25


Nasdaq 100 -0.6% +1.8% to 26,571.0


Dow Jones +0.3% +0.82% to 50,638.0


The rebound spread overseas. Japan's Nikkei 225 gained 1.4% and South Korea's Kospi rose nearly 1% on Thursday, with SoftBank, Kioxia, Samsung and SK Hynix among the stocks that gained or recovered, per Saxo. European bourses opened firmer and held their gains through the session, with Italy's FTSE MIB up 2.1%, in what Newsquawk described as a catch-up to the rebound in US equities on Wednesday.


## Treasury Futures Slip 4 Ticks as Haven Demand Fades


Treasuries rallied during Wednesday's volatile session. The 10-year yield fell as much as 10 basis points to 4.83% before closing near 4.85%, the 2-year yield eased to about 4.63%, and the[iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/tlt/) rose 0.92%, according to Saxo.


With cash Treasury trading shut for Thanksgiving, Treasury futures slipped 4 ticks on Thursday within a narrow 106-28+ to 107-04 range, as reported by Newsquawk. German Bunds fell 45 ticks, and global fixed income held a bearish bias as Dutch TTF gas and crude prices climbed. Cash Treasury markets close early on Friday, Saxo noted.


## Copper Rebounds From Its Lowest Since Last December


Copper had been one of the clearest casualties of the sell-off. March copper futures touched $5.31 a pound, the lowest since last December, before recovering to $5.45, leaving the metal on course for a monthly decline of around 17%, per Saxo.


Prices firmed on Thursday as sentiment improved. Three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange traded within a $11,826.00 to $12,092.53 per tonne range alongside the improved risk sentiment, according to Newsquawk. Spot gold was a little lower in a $3,551 to $3,607 an ounce range, stabilizing after the prior day's gains.


Crude also moved higher, with WTI and Brent up about 1.3% and 1.7% respectively, as Newsquawk cited reports suggesting that Kuwait was struck by Iranian drones.


## Core PCE at 3.3% Keeps a December Fed Hike in Play


The macro backdrop still leans hawkish. October PCE inflation rose to 3.8% year on year, its highest in five months, while[core PCE came in at 3.3%](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/gold-price-falls-below-3500-core-pce/) against a 3.2% forecast, Saxo reported. Q3 GDP was revised up to 4.3% annualized from 3.4%, and weekly jobless claims fell to 189,000.


Against that data, markets price a December Fed rate increase as highly likely, according to Saxo. Investing.com pointed to growing doubts over whether the debt-fueled spending frenzy on technology can be sustained as interest rates rise, a concern behind the deep, extended tech losses through October and November.


Trade policy is another overhang. Proposed Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies include up to 20% on China on top of existing duties and 15% on the EU and Japan, with comments due by January 5, 2027, per Saxo.
